tast.video.DecodeAccel*: Don't disable video frame validator in tests. This CL makes a small change to the parameters passed to the new video decoder tests. Currently --disable_validator is used to switch from the frame validator to the thumbnail tests on platforms that don't support import mode. This is done as a fallback since frame validation is only supported on platforms supporting import mode. crrev.com/c/1688769 makes the test automatically detect import mode support. crrev.com/c/1688493 changes the logic of the --disable_validator parameter to disable both the video frame validator (on platforms supporting import mode) and the thumbnail test (on platforms only supporting allocate mode). This CL updates the parameters passed to the binary to reflect the new behavior. Note: Only submit after the next Chrome uprev containing CL 1688769 and 1688493. diagnostics: Change structure of EcEvent Before, the payload of an EcEvent was just an opaque array. To allow for parsing the event for certain flags which should cause notifications, re-structure the payload array to packed structs. Also fix the meaning of the |size| field in EcEvent. Before, the |size| field of an EcEvent was interpreted to mean "The number of words in the payload array." This is incorrect, the EC will fill this field with "The number of following words in the struct", AKA including the |type| word, AKA one more than we thought. With the incorrect interpretation, some valid EcEvents are filtered out from being sent in WilcoDtcSupportdCore::SendGrpcEcEventToWilcoDtc. This patch corrects the interpretation of |size| when we construct EcEvents and decode them for making gRPC calls. TEST=unit tests BUG=b:126320709, chromium:972105 Change-Id: Idd69f89682be0b10723465ef34a4687c6ef0508c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1705336 Tested-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Trent Begin <tbegin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

check_ethernet: promote rescan_usb_hubs to recovery_method Today, we may run rescan_usb_hubs a number of times just because it's part of the find_ethernet_interfaces() function. This isn't really a good idea for cases that aren't recoverable -- it wastes a bunch of time and caues confusing "bouncy" behavior. We can improve this by sharing the 'recovery_method' logic, which (a) tries the recovery action (b) checks whether that action did anything useful (c) if so, retry connectivity diagnostics; if not, try the next method immediately. This pattern matches what we want for rescan_usb_hubs anyway: just try it once, if there were no operational links; don't re-try it several times as an implicit part of looking for devices. This eliminates any logic in find_ethernet_devices(), so we just alias with search_devices(). A few additions to rescan_usb_hubs() along the way: * re-check whether there are any devices (search_devices()) after running, to determine our "success"; poll over 15 seconds -- in addition to kernel hub enumeration, it can take some time for usb_guard to authorize the device * factor out some delays until after we iterate over all hubs * add a sanity check in case the "${usbhub}/... globbing doesn't match anything BUG=chromium:982940 TEST=manually-induced failures (e.g., delete interface), see how script responds Change-Id: I118db269002ebba9267446bfbbdba7b3bf6e938e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1714129 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org>

check_ethernet: improve find_ssh_client for IPv6 This function had a number of problems: (a) doesn't satisfy its description: it could print more than 1 IP, which its callers wouldn't really like (b) it has this minor shellcheck warning: "SC1004: This backslash+linefeed is literal. Break outside single quotes if you just want to break the line." (c) it only handles IPv4 properly (IPv6 has colons in the address, so we were only dumping the first hextet) Fixes applied here: * netstat -l (listening) -- contradicts our search for "established" * netstat -p (program name) -- we ignore this * netstat -a (listening and non-listening) -- again, we're only looking for "established" * netstat -t -- add this, to limit the output netstat has to generate * netstat -W -- need wide printing, to fit IPv6 addresses * convert awk pattern to match columns more precisely, instead of a regex across the entire line * only look for the last colon when stripping the port (i.e., dead:beef:...:22 -> dead:beef:...) * exit after the first match Also, while netstat sort of gives us a time-ordered listing of connections, it doesn't sort across different protocols (e.g., v4 vs. v6). So just drop the "first" comment -- it's not really important to the logic, as long as this finds some valid address. BUG=none TEST=none Change-Id: I4d92d22572c5fd3bc8f85b97749a38cace8a0fb9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1714130 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org>

tast-tests: vm: Extended the CrostiniPre to allow for an image artifact To prevent network-based flake, we would like to migrate crostini tests so that they use a pre-built image artifact where possible, rather than downloading the image. We refactor the CrostiniPre so that it can source the image either from a download or from the data dependency. This is a workaround suggested by nya@ which still requires us to list the data dependency for every artifact-based crostini test. As a result of this change, we make several refactorings to the tests that involve the artifact: - We use the component "crostini" rather than "vm" to distinguish from tests for termina, or pluginvm - We adopt a parametric style, namely that crostini tests should run both via-download and via-build-artifact. In discussion with tast-users we are modelling the parameterization after the videos/ tests. This change affects both vm.CrostiniStartBasic (which is now crostini.Sanity*) and vm.CrostiniAudioSanity (which is now crostini.AudioSanityArtifact). BUG=chromium:979074,chromium:980048,chromium:981426 TEST=tast -verbose run ${DUT} "crostini.*" Change-Id: Ie67e8d5abbee5bad8f30784a2ea7b860ec807eae Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1679771 Tested-by: Nic Hollingum <hollingum@google.com> Commit-Ready: Nic Hollingum <hollingum@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

faft: Make firmware_FWupdate use current firmware The test was previously using the images contained in the built-in /usr/sbin/chromeos-firmwareupdate, but that could trigger an unwanted downgrade, if the device was running a newer firmware before the test started. The test now undoes any modifications left over from previous runs, at the start of the test. There's logic to restore the firmware at the end of the test, but it is possible for that logic to not run. That's part of why it's important to keep the running version unchanged. Make timestamps on gestures match incoming events In the gesture library, we use MSC_TIMESTAMP from the touch controller to adjust the timestamp from the browser, allowing more accurate timestamp deltas. However, some skew can occur between the two clock sources, causing issues in the browser. This CL adjusts the timestamps after the gestures are produced to more closely match the original timestamp for events. cros-disks: Simplify Process and subclasses Added some consts. System call execve() and C wrapper function execv() take their argv parameter as char* const* and not as char** Removed args parameter from method Process::StartImpl(). These args used to be passed as mutable reference to a vector (although the passed vector was never meant to be modified). But this was not even necessary since StartImpl() implementations can access the arguments through Process::GetArguments(). This also simplifies Process::Start(), where GetArguments() was called for its side effects but its return value was ignored. Process::GetArguments() is unit-tested. But the args parameter passed to Process::StartImpl() was never checked by unit tests. Removing it simply removes a source of potential errors and confusion. It also potentially opens up bugs where the udev context is null but we pass it into udev library functions anyway. Make this harder to get wrong by combining the construction steps into one, so a Udev object always has a valid udev context. Then move to the new version of this in mist.
